name: Data Center Design Fundamentals
audience: Facility engineers, design consultants, and project leads planning new builds or major expansions.

dc.hook: Design data center facilities that scale — from site selection to redundancy strategy.
dc.description: Every high-availability data center starts as a set of design decisions — and the wrong ones are expensive to unwind after concrete is poured. This course walks through the full design lifecycle used by enterprise facility teams: international standards (ANSI/TIA-942, ISO 14644), site selection criteria, thermal design principles, power architecture, and the redundancy trade-offs (N, N+1, N+2, 2N) that determine both uptime and capital cost. You'll work through real design case studies, thermal modeling concepts, and ROI analysis frameworks used to justify facility investment to executive stakeholders. Rather than teaching a single vendor's playbook, the course focuses on the trade-off reasoning behind design choices, so you can evaluate proposals, vet vendor recommendations, and defend your own design decisions with data. By the end, you'll be able to read a facility design proposal critically, model redundancy options against budget constraints, and build the financial case for an expansion or new build.
outcomes: Apply ANSI/TIA-942 and ISO 14644 standards to real site and facility design decisions
Evaluate site selection criteria for power, connectivity, climate, and risk
Compare N, N+1, N+2, and 2N redundancy models on cost and uptime trade-offs
Build thermal design fundamentals into early-stage facility planning
Construct a capital ROI case for a facility expansion or new build
Certificate of completion on finish
Self-paced — start and stop anytime
Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider

name: Tier Infrastructure Fundamentals

dc.description: The TIER classification system (I through IV) is the industry's shorthand for facility reliability — but understanding what actually separates a TIER III facility from a TIER IV one takes more than reading a definitions page. This is practical benchmarking knowledge: understand where your facility sits today, what it would take to move up a TIER level, and how to communicate that gap to stakeholders.

Apply infrastructure scoring methods to benchmark an existing facility
